about: Pass 9 (2026-10-10), more image, video, TTS and STT models. Candidates only; nothing in data/ was edited. (3) Hugging Face TTS model cards created since 2026-06-15 with open licences were scanned for comparison tables with catalogue names: two Apache-2.0 cards run Freya-TR-Eval (Turkish) themselves, which scores Eleven v4 / v4 Turbo, Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS / Flash-Lite TTS and Coqui GlowTTS Turkish (the last three previously unscored). (4) Every pinned speech ledger source was compared with its current HEAD. Validated with apply-pass2.mjs + npm run import + node scripts/check.ts --validate-only on a scratch copy of the 2026-10-10 working tree (1,432 models): +45 models, +99 results, +4 benchmarks, 5 new ledger entries and 1 add_match; every new model ends in the main comparison set of its category.

benchmarks.name: Freya-TR-Eval Turkish TTS intelligibility (WER, faster-whisper large-v3, 8 kHz band)
benchmarks.setup: Freya-TR-Eval (freyavoice/freya-tr-eval, CC BY 4.0): 495 raw Turkish sentences (everyday text with numbers, dates, money, abbreviations). Each system speaks every sentence (3 seeds or takes, default/fixed voice); clips are band-limited to 8 kHz and back to 16 kHz, transcribed by Whisper large-v3 (faster-whisper, beam 5, language tr), reference and hypothesis get Freya's Turkish normalisation, and corpus WER is computed over the whole set with jiwer; the score is the mean over the 3 seeds, as printed. Two evaluator runs: the EMA Lightning card ('Our runs', RTX 4090) and Patientdesk.ai's independent re-run (EMA Lightning's published eval.py, NVIDIA L4) printed on the Antalia-2 Mini card.
caveats: Single-language (Turkish) intelligibility only; says nothing about naturalness or voice cloning.
Automatic ASR-judged metric with one ASR model; both evaluators also build Turkish TTS models (their own rows are by: lab).
Cloud APIs run with default voices (ElevenLabs 'George', Gemini 'Kore'); cloning systems use the Anka male reference clip.
Coqui GlowTTS input is lowercased the Turkish way first (the front end that model needs).

benchmarks.name: MultiTextEdit cross-lingual text-in-image editing (SemAvg, LVM judge)
benchmarks.setup: MultiTextEdit (Harbin Institute of Technology, arXiv:2605.08163v2, CC BY 4.0): 3,600 text-in-image editing instances across 12 typologically diverse languages/scripts (insertion, replacement, deletion of rendered text), each with a human-annotated reference image. An LVM judge scores instruction following, text accuracy, visual consistency, layout preservation and language/script fidelity on 0-5 (two-stage protocol for script fidelity; human agreement QWK 0.76 on 240 samples). SemAvg = mean of the five dimensions over all instances, as printed in Table 3; stored as SemAvg/5. The authors ran every system themselves with the provider's official pipeline and highest-quality recommended settings (open models on 8xA800; proprietary via official APIs).
benchmarks.score_unit: fraction of the 0-5 judge scale (printed SemAvg / 5)
caveats: Judge model not named in the text; scores are LVM-judged, validated against one native speaker per language.
Thinking-enabled variants are listed as separate settings; for BAGEL the thinking row is used (highest reasoning setting), as on Edit-Compass.
Step1X-Edit rows not imported: the paper does not say which Step1X-Edit version (the thinking variant implies v1.2).

benchmarks.name: What-If World causal-intervention video generation (APEO paired average, Gemini 3.1 Pro judge)
benchmarks.setup: What-If World (UCLA / University of Tennessee, arXiv:2605.27589v1, CC BY 4.0): 319 driving (nuScenes) and robot-manipulation (DROID) scenes; from one real initial frame each model generates two videos for a minimally different prompt pair (an intervention on one causal variable: force, timing, friction, material, obstacle, alignment). Gemini 3.1 Pro judges Adherence, Physics, Environment and Outcome on the pair; pAvg (the paper's primary paired metric) is the mean paired pass rate, as printed in Table 2; stored /100. Open models run by the authors with their public default inference settings on RTX A6000s; closed models via hosted APIs (kie.ai).
caveats: Closed models accessed through the kie.ai reseller; vendor tiers not stated.

Not imported: CogVideoX1.5-5B (T2V vs I2V checkpoint not stated), 'Cosmos-Predict2-2B' (the table names Predict2 but the citation is the Cosmos-Predict2.5 report), 'Kling 3.0' (cited as the Kling-Omni report, so Kling 3.0 vs Kling 3.0 Omni is unclear).

benchmarks.name: CRONOS counterfactual rigid-body physics (I2V success rate)
benchmarks.setup: CRONOS (University of Freiburg / MPI Informatics / CISPA, arXiv:2605.23699v1, CC BY 4.0): synthetic rigid-body scenes (falls, collisions) with controlled counterfactual interventions; each model continues the scene from the first frame (I2V). Per-video metrics (background stability, motion similarity to the simulator ground truth, appearance and 3D-shape stability, physical plausibility) are thresholded with human-calibrated cut-offs; a video counts as a success only if every metric passes. Score = fraction of successful videos averaged over all videos, as printed in Table 1 (I2V block). All models run by the authors with open weights.
caveats: Success rates are near the floor for weaker models (0.01-0.02), so the test separates mainly the top models.
Only the I2V block is used; the V2V block (five conditioning frames, Cosmos and MAGI-1 only) is a different setting.
CogVideoX1.5-5B row not imported (the catalogue has no CogVideoX1.5 I2V checkpoint entry).
